verdict.rationale: kitty's own docs list startup sessions for specifying working environments, alongside programmable tabs, splits and layouts and script control. A hands-on user confirms default startup tabs are easy to set up, but reports that session-file arguments are barely documented. missing for 10: detailed documentation of session-file syntax and how layouts are declared in it, explicit evidence of opening a full project workspace with one command (e.g. a documented --session invocation), and better-documented session-file arguments.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can define startup sessions and window layouts in config or scripts so a project workspace opens in one command

citations.quote: Use startup sessions to specify working environments; Programmable tabs, splits and multiple layouts to manage windows.
kitty can be controlled from scripts or the shell prompt. You can open new windows, send arbitrary text input to any window, change the title of windows and tabs, etc.
easy to set up default startup tabs, unlike gnome-terminal; CLI tools take different arguments in session files, barely documented
